summary: BENNETT is an end-to-end, open-source decision-support and early warning ecosystem that translates complex Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) telemetry from the NASA-ISRO SAR (NISAR) mission into actionable territorial intelligence. Addressing the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge, BENNETT tracks millimeter-scale surface deformation (creep), dielectric soil moisture shifts, and interferometric coherence loss across 21 high-risk hillside zones in La Paz and El Alto, Bolivia. Our custom Python/HDF5 filtering pipeline reduces raw 17–19 GB NISAR scenes by up to 98%, feeding a deterministic Multi-Factor Territorial Attention Index and our SLIDEGUARD_SOUP ML engine. The platform integrates three operational components: a bilingual (EN/ES) interactive web digital twin built with React 19 and MapLibre GL featuring a weather Scenario Simulator and automated PDF technical reports; a high-performance Rust (Axum/Tokio) backend serving REST and real-time WebSocket streams; and a native Kotlin (Jetpack Compose) Android app delivering instant traffic-light risk indicators and emergency push alarms to citizens and authorities.
details:
What it does & How it works BENNETT is a multi-tiered geospatial intelligence and early-warning ecosystem designed to anticipate slow-moving slope deformation (creep) and prevent catastrophic landslides using active radar remote sensing from the NASA-ISRO SAR (NISAR) mission:

  1. Selective NISAR HDF5 Pipeline & Active Radar Physics: Raw NISAR scenes reach 17–19 GB per pass. Our specialized extractor (filter_nisar_landslide.py) strips internal hardware telemetry while preserving critical /science/LSAR/ variables (L-band $\lambda \approx 24\text{ cm}$ co-pol $HH$, cross-pol $HV$, unwrapped interferometric phase $\Delta \phi$, coherence $\gamma$, incidenceAngle, and layoverShadowMask), achieving an 85%–98% size reduction. L-band wavelengths penetrate vegetation canopies to detect volumetric soil moisture ($\theta_v$) and dielectric permittivity ($\epsilon_r$) surges prior to Mohr-Coulomb shear failure, while Differential InSAR tracks sub-centimeter Line-of-Sight (LOS) displacement over 12-day orbital cycles.
  2. Multi-Factor Territorial Attention Index & ML Bridge: Each monitored slope is evaluated on a $0\text{--}100$ deterministic scale ($I = \min(100, 30 f_v + 25 f_p + 15 f_h + 15 f_s + 15 f_g)$) combining InSAR velocity, GPM IMERG cumulative precipitation, soil moisture, terrain gradient, and local lithology, complemented by our Python/Scikit-learn/LoRA engine (SLIDEGUARD_SOUP).
  3. Interactive Web Digital Twin: Deployed athttps://challenge-dancing.vercel.app, the web UI offers a Multi-Layer Interactive Map (MapLibre GL), a Scenario Simulator to stress-test slopes under severe storms, an Inspection Prioritization Ranking, live ASF DAAC orbital pass queries, CSV open-data exports, and printable PDF technical reports.
  4. High-Performance Backend & Citizen Mobile App: A Hexagonal-architecture Rust backend (Axum/Tokio) serves REST endpoints and broadcasts real-time alerts via WebSockets (/ws/alerts) to a native Kotlin (Jetpack Compose) Android app that provides citizens and transit operators with a live risk traffic light and full-screen audible/visual emergency alarms.

Benefits & Intended Impact Piloted across 21 critical hillside sectors in La Paz and El Alto, Bolivia (spanning extreme elevations from $3,200$ to $4,100\text{ m a.s.l.}$ over fragile La Paz, Colluvial, and Calvario geological formations), BENNETT transforms isolated terabytes of radar data into an accessible operational tool. It shifts municipal disaster management from reactive post-collapse rescue to proactive, prioritized field inspections and community preparedness.
